meta.description: Adopting change instead of just shipping it: a UX case study of the Unistellar app redesign.

cover.title: Reducing friction
cover.subtitle: Turning a task-driven experience into a user-driven one.
cover.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Unistellar app on a tablet, showing the celestial object catalog grid with the Moon and Jupiter.

hero.title: Adopt the change, don’t just ship it

context.title: The context
context.text: We just shipped V2, designed without any chance for upfront user testing — an ambitious visual redesign that was objectively a success on its own terms. Once live, the first feedback comes in.
context.quote: I was super motivated to get started, but now I feel completely lost — I don’t know where to go next.

issue.title: The problem
issue.text1: Version two marked a complete visual overhaul of the product. The interface was objectively more modern, better structured.
issue.text2: And yet, on release, the welcome was cold: long-time users weren’t asking for a new experience, they wanted their bearings back. An interface judged better, but experienced as worse.

method.title: The method
paragraphs: With no dedicated budget or formal access to users, I put together field test sessions on short notice.

The focus was new users discovering the product for the first time: solving their blockers would also improve the experience for everyone else, by extension. A simple but rigorous protocol: screen capture, video recording of the scene, thinking aloud, then a hot debrief questionnaire.
method.journeyIntro:
From these observations, I reconstructed the key moments of the journey.
Connecting, orienting, discovering the catalog — and for each one identified the friction points as well as the user's emotional state at that moment.

journey.label: Connexion
journey.title: Create Actions That Inspire and Engage
journey.text: Some app actions fail to connect emotionally or offer practical value, creating unnecessary frustration and lowering user satisfaction.

journey.label: Orientation
journey.title: Be a Guide for Users Through Their Discovery
journey.text: When faced with an overwhelming number of objects to observe, users often feel confused and uncertain about where to begin. Offering curated suggestions can eliminate the "blank page" effect and help them engage meaningfully.

journey.label: Select Target
journey.title: Guide Users to Quick Insights
journey.text: Interaction zones has a lack of hierarchy and meaningful associations, leaving users confused when trying to complete an action. Clear guidance and structured design are critical to enhancing usability and enabling efficient navigation.

journey.label: Enhanced Vision
journey.title: A Stagnant Experience Deteriorates Over Time
journey.text: Once the action is triggered, no further interaction with the image is possible. The user becomes passive, leading to boredom and disengagement.

quotes.text: So can I focus it now?.
Let's try pointing at something? No, I wanted to go to the brightest star.
Well I'm trying, yeah I see I've pointed at a star, and I'd like to know what I'm actually looking at.
I don't know where I'm supposed to go…
No but I... OK, and how do I know it's found it,
I don't think I recognized that was a joystick… Actually, I had trouble telling that you can steer in different directions with it… [I wanted to see] A button instead.
Azimuth, I have no idea what that means…
So starting the observation… oh my god, I'm totally lost here!

facilitation.intro: Facing a development team that was initially skeptical, the debrief happened in two steps:
steps: Presenting the problem alone, with no preconceived solution, to spark collective thinking,
facilitation.text: This approach turned an initial "there's nothing we can do" into real engagement, by showing that design could make the subject exciting rather than constraining.

results.title: The results
results.text: V3 simplified sign-in, guided orientation step by step, and put the catalog back at the center of the experience. NPS improved significantly, confirmed by additional usability tests.

learning.title: The learning
learning.text: A paradox appeared after the fact: long-time users, who had never really run into the connection and orientation issues, didn't perceive the improvement, even though the data showed a clear drop in blockers. A reminder that perceived experience and usage metrics don't always tell the same story, and that solving a problem measured through users and data doesn't guarantee it will match the user's felt experience.
